item.title: Java CSV Parsing: Exploring Libraries for Reading and Writing CSV Files
item.description:
“Java CSV Parsing: Exploring Libraries for Reading and Writing CSV Files”

Handling Comma-Separated Values (CSV) data in Java presents a common challenge. While the format appears simple, variations in delimiters, escaping characters, and specific file structures (like those from Excel) can make direct string manipulation error-prone. Utilizing dedicated libraries offers a more robust and maintainable approach.

Several third-party libraries have emerged to address this need, each with its own strengths. Let’s explore some of the most recommended options and their capabilities.

item.title: Python CSV Writing: Avoid Extra Blank Lines
item.description:
“Python CSV Writing: Avoid Extra Blank Lines”

When working with Python’s csv module to write data to CSV files, particularly on Windows, you might encounter an issue where extra blank lines appear between rows. This often happens due to how Python’s text file handling interacts with the default line endings expected by the csv module. Let’s explore the common causes and effective solutions for this problem.

The core of the issue lies in newline character translation. On Windows, text files typically use (carriage return followed by newline) as line endings. However, when writing CSV files in Python’s default text mode, the csv.writer might introduce its own line endings (like ), and then the operating system’s text mode translation process can convert these to , leading to a sequence, which the CSV reader interprets as an extra blank line.

item.title: Top 20 Methods to Determine Total Row Count in a CSV File Using Python
item.description:
Top 20 Methods to Determine Total Row Count in a CSV File Using Python

Counting the total number of rows in a CSV file can be essential for data analysis, reporting, or handling large datasets, especially when working within a Python environment such as Django or Flask. This guide explores 20 effective methods to ascertain the total number of rows in a CSV file using Python, providing practical code examples and discussing performance where relevant.
